To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the prevalence of isolated clinical hypertension (ICH, defined by a persistently normal day-time or ambulatory 24 h-blood pressure in the presence a persistently elevated office blood pressure) in a large cohort of never-treated hypertensive subjects was 7.6% (95% CI: 5.9-9.4%).
the prevalence of ICH is lower than expected, and that ICH is not a stable condition, as the prevalence of ICP changes over time.

the prevalence of isolated clinical hypertension (ICH), defined by the criteria suggested by major hypertension societies, was 7% in never treated grade 1 and grade 2 hypertensives and that ICH is not a stable condition, with a limited short-term reliability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reliability of a single ABP recording in the detection of ICH.
the reliability of the definition of isolated clinical hypertension based on a single ambulatory blood pressure recording.
the reliability of the definition of ICH based on the criteria currently recommended in the main hypertension guidelines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a single ABP recording is not sufficient to diagnose ICH.
the diagnosis of ICH based on ABPM has limited short-term reproducible and that repeated ABPM recordings are needed to confirm the diagnosis of ICPH
ICH is a condition which should be confirmed by repeated ABPM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the current definition of Isolated Clinical Hypertension based on a single ambulatory blood pressure measurement (ABPM) has a low reproducibility, and repeated ABPM recordings are recommended to correctly diagnose this condition.
a patient who has a single 24h BP monitoring with normal values and a normal clinic BP is likely to have a low cardiovascular risk.
the current guidelines for the definition of ICH are not reliable.

the classification of ICP on the basis of one ABPM, using cut-off values proposed by major hypertension guidelines has a limited short- term reproducibility.
a single 24 h ABPM recording should not be used to diagnose ICH, and that repeated ABPM recordings are needed.
